note: m1400-m1301 window agent, 2 Nov 2026. (1) The Khabur Valley (Hasaka) stays Mitanni's until Assyria takes Washukanni (assyria ledger 15, mitanni ledger 12, -1300): events 0-1, keyframe_overrides 0-2, tint events 2-3. (2) Three dossier keyframes lack the 'to' their notes state, so the compiler unions them with the later keyframes to -1301: mitanni_-1400 (to -1351), new-kingdom-of-egypt_-1400 (to -1353), keyframe_overrides 3-4; with hittites_-1345 widened to ledger 4's region (override 5). (3) Canaan keeps the Egyptian vassal tint after -1352 (event 4).

region.text: the Khabur Valley, which the named region 'Assyria' sweeps in but the page does not give Ashur-uballit I

events.note: Ashur-uballit I 'annexed Mitanni territory in the middle of the 14th century BC' (Mitanni page; no Khabur or Washukanni named), and after the Hittite war 'the kingdom had by now been reduced to the Khabur Valley'. The Khabur cities fall to Assyria under Adad-nirari I and Wasashatta, c. 1300 (assyria ledger 15). So the 82 Hasaka cells that the region 'Assyria' of ledger 14 took in -1363 go back to Mitanni.

region.text: the Khabur Valley, the Mitanni heartland round Washukanni

events.note: Undoes the Hasaka share of mitanni ledger 5: the Khabur Valley is not among the 'Mitanni territory' that Ashur-uballit I annexed on the page, and it is still the Mitanni rump after 1327 ('reduced to the Khabur Valley').

region.text: the Khabur Valley round Washukanni (Tell Fekheriye), 'on the headwaters of the Khabur River'

events.note: c. 1330: Shattiwaza's Mitanni is a Hittite vassal. 'installed Shattiwaza, the son of Tushratta, as their vassal king of Mitanni in the late 14th century BC'; 'Shattiwaza reigned c. 1330-1305 BC'. Washukanni, the seat, 'on the headwaters of the Khabur River', lies in Hasaka, which ledger 8 (Cliopatria's 1300 shape) leaves out, so the Khabur part of the rump is tinted with the rest.

region.text: the Khabur Valley round Washukanni (Tell Fekheriye), 'on the headwaters of the Khabur River'

events.note: c. 1305: Shattiwaza's reign ends and 'Adad-nirari claims to have captured King Shattuara and brought him to Ashur, where he took an oath as a vassal' (the page). Closes the Hittite suzerainty over the Khabur part as ledger 10 does for the rest of the rump.

region.text: the Canaanite city-states of the Amarna letters

events.note: The Amarna letters, written 'no more than 30 years in the middle of the 14th century BC' to the desertion of Amarna in 1332 BC, are 'correspondence between the Egyptian administration and its representatives in Canaan and Amurru', and the Habiru were 'attacking Egyptian vassal territories throughout Canaan'. The -1352 keyframe keeps Canaan 'as vassal tint', but the ledger's vassal_end of the Syrian cities (ledger 10) leaves it drawn as direct land from -1352; reopen the vassal tint over Canaan.

correction.text: the 1400 shape without the eastern Tigris lands, with the Khabur Valley kept

keyframe_overrides.why: The page says that after the Hittite war 'The kingdom had by now been reduced to the Khabur Valley' and that the Assyrians took Washukanni, Kahat and the other Khabur cities only under Wasashatta (c. 1285-1265 BC); Ashur-uballit I (1365-1330 BC) 'annexed Mitanni territory in the middle of the 14th century BC' without the page naming the Khabur. The dossier's own note says Washukanni 'remained Mitanni's seat', but Cliopatria's 1300 shape (37.3-40.35 E) lies west of the Khabur, so the compile handed Hasaka's 82 cells to Assyria in -1363 and -1350.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1400 shape, unchanged, valid for -1400..-1351 only

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's note reads 'valid for -1400..-1351 only' ('Ashur-uballit I (1365-1330) annexed Mitanni territory in the middle of the 14th century BC' and 'The Hittite-Syrian war is dated to 1345 BC'), but the entry has no 'to', so the compiler gives it Cliopatria's span to -1301 and unions it with the later keyframes mitanni_-1350, -1345 and -1327. Mitanni then claims its whole 1400 shape in every year to -1301 and the succession rule hands the contested cells to Assyria and the Hittites (666 cell-years of assyria/mitanni conflicts). 'to' is set to -1351, the year before mitanni_-1350 begins.

correction.text: the Thutmose III shape without the Aleppo region, valid -1447..-1353 (Aleppo was never Egyptian, so there is no loss to Mitanni); from -1352 see keyframe -1352

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's note reads 'valid -1447..-1353' (the Thutmose III shape without the Aleppo region), but the entry has no 'to', so the compiler gives it Cliopatria's span to -1301 and unions it with new-kingdom-of-egypt_-1352 (Egypt, Nubia and Canaan, 'Egypt had not held Kadesh since the time of Akhenaten'). Egypt then keeps claiming Syria north of Canaan, to Kadesh, in every year to -1301 (about 60 cells round Damascus stay Egyptian and direct, and the Egypt-Hittite, -Amurru and -Ugarit conflicts recur). 'to' is set to -1353, the year before new-kingdom-of-egypt_-1352 begins.

union.text: the 1400 Anatolian shape plus the Hittite conquests in Syria after Suppiluliuma I's war

correction.text: the 1400 Anatolian shape, the Hittite conquests in Syria, and the Mitanni lands west of the Euphrates that ledger 4 gives to the Hittites

keyframe_overrides.why: The page: Suppiluliuma 'subjugated Aleppo, Mukish, Niya, Arahtu, Qatna and Nuhasshi. This campaign was fought in 1345 BC'. The dossier's ledger 4 gives the Hittites 'Aleppo, Mukish (Alalakh) and the other Mitanni lands west of the Euphrates' in -1345, but the keyframe takes only the 1400 shape plus the part of the 1300 shape inside the Levant region, so the keyframe snap released about 50 cells of Gaziantep, Adiyaman and Kilis that the ledger had just given (and Mitanni's keyframe then took them back). The keyframe now holds the ledger's own region.
